entities.name: Battle of Guadalete
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Guadalete was a pivotal 711 CE clash between the Visigothic Kingdom and the Umayyad Caliphate, resulting in a decisive Umayyad victory that led to the fall of the Visigothic Kingdom and the Umayyad conquest of the Iberian Peninsula.

This cataclysmic event occurred on July 19, 711, and had far-reaching implications for the future of Iberia and beyond. The Visigothic Kingdom, once a powerful force in the region, was severely weakened, paving the way for the Umayyad Caliphate's dominance.

The consequences of the Battle of Guadalete were profound, as the Umayyad conquest of the Iberian Peninsula marked the beginning of a new era in the region's history. The event also had a lasting impact on the cultural and linguistic landscape of the peninsula, shaping the course of Western civilization.

The legacy of the Battle of Guadalete continues to be felt today, with its effects evident in the complex tapestry of cultures, languages, and empires that have shaped the modern world.

As the 8th-century historian Ibn Al-Qutiya noted, 'The Battle of Guadalete was a turning point in the history of the Iberian Peninsula, marking the beginning of a new era of Islamic rule and the decline of the Visigothic Kingdom.'
